Adds an Electron-based `@clickclack/desktop` app, desktop GitHub OAuth endpoints and docs, web bridge hooks, generated assets, root scripts, lockfile updates, and a three-OS packaging workflow.

Reproducibility: yes. for the review finding: source inspection shows a cold-start Quick Compose action can send `desktop:quick-compose` before the Svelte `onMount` listener exists. I did not run Electron locally, but the lost-IPC path is clear at the current PR head.

target.title: [codex] add native desktop apps for macOS, Windows, and Linux
target.body:
## Summary

Adds first-party Electron apps for macOS, Windows, and Linux. ClickClack's hosted/self-hosted web app remains the canonical product; the desktop shell adds OS integration and a secure system-browser GitHub sign-in handoff.

The earlier embedded OAuth approach has been replaced. Clicking **Continue with GitHub** now opens the user's default browser, reuses its existing GitHub session/passkeys/password manager/2FA, then returns to the same ClickClack app through `clickclack://auth/callback`.

## Native capabilities

- Native notifications that deep-link to the relevant channel or DM.
- Dock/taskbar badges, Windows overlay badge, and tray unread state.
- Close-to-tray background presence while realtime activity stays connected.
- Quick Compose from the app menu with `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+K`.
- `clickclack://` deep links with cold-start and single-instance routing.
- Native downloads, external-link routing, spellcheck, and context menus.
- Launch-at-login controls on macOS and Windows.
- Persistent window placement and a native settings window.
- Hosted ClickClack by default, configurable HTTPS self-hosted origins, and loopback HTTP for local development.

## System-browser authentication

1. Electron creates a high-entropy verifier and SHA-256 challenge.
2. The desktop bridge opens `/api/auth/github/desktop/start?code_challenge=...` in the default browser.
3. GitHub completes the existing server-side OAuth flow. Pending desktop state is held only in short-lived HTTP-only browser cookies, so abandoned public starts consume no server-side state.
4. The callback redirects to `clickclack://auth/callback?code=...` with an opaque five-minute grant. GitHub access tokens and ClickClack session tokens never enter the custom-protocol URL.
5. The initiating app redeems the grant with its verifier against the exact server origin. Redemption is same-origin checked, verifier-bound, atomic, and single-use.
6. Electron confirms the persistent `cc_session` cookie and reloads the original window as the signed-in workspace.

The existing web OAuth flow is unchanged. A legacy desktop navigation interception remains only as a migration path for older rendered pages and immediately transfers the request to the system browser.

## Security boundaries

- Context isolation, sandboxing, web security, and disabled Node integration stay enabled.
- The preload exposes a small typed bridge; no arbitrary IPC, shell, filesystem, environment, or credential access.
- Renderer capabilities are restricted to the configured ClickClack origin, with IPC sender validation in the main process.
- Remote navigation and GitHub OAuth open externally; GitHub is never embedded in Electron.
- Remote origins require HTTPS; plain HTTP is limited to loopback development.
- Permission requests from remote content are denied.
- OAuth callback query strings remain excluded from request logs.

## Packaging and CI

- macOS: DMG and ZIP for Intel and Apple Silicon.
- Windows: NSIS installer and ZIP for x64.
- Linux: AppImage and DEB for x64.
- Cross-platform ClickClack icon set: ICNS, ICO, PNG, and tray artwork.
- Desktop CI matrix tests, type-checks, packages, and uploads unsigned preview artifacts on all three operating systems.

## Web, API, and documentation

- Connects realtime unread state, active routes, deep-link navigation, Quick Compose, notifications, and system-browser sign-in to the desktop bridge.
- Adds documented desktop start/consume endpoints to OpenAPI and regenerates the TypeScript SDK declarations.
- Updates desktop, authentication, development, security, packaging, and native-feature docs.
- Updates the user-facing changelog.

## Validation

- `pnpm check`
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm test:e2e` — 41 passed
- `actionlint .github/workflows/desktop.yml`
- `CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false pnpm --filter @clickclack/desktop run pack`
- Packaged macOS behavior pass: launch, hosted sign-in surface, server validation, insecure remote HTTP rejection, close-to-tray, and restore.
- Desktop OAuth regression pass: cross-origin consume rejection, wrong-verifier rejection without burning the grant, successful cookie handoff, one-time redemption, and replay rejection.
- Structured Codex autoreview: clean after fixing the identified public-start resource-exhaustion path.
- Production rollout: Cloudflare Worker version `e773cf41-ea6e-42c8-9544-2571131316c2` serves the new container on `app.clickclack.chat`, `clickclack.chat`, and `www.clickclack.chat`; the retired single-host fallback runs merge revision `4ba07ed24119`.
- Fresh-profile live E2E with Computer Use and the existing Chrome profile: the app stayed visible with its browser-completion message, GitHub reused the browser session without credential entry, and the same Electron window became a connected ClickClack workspace.
- GitHub Actions: Docker Image, Go, TypeScript, Playwright E2E, macOS Desktop, Windows Desktop, and Linux Desktop all pass on head `74bb78564e42`.

## Distribution follow-up

CI artifacts are unsigned previews. Production distribution still needs platform signing credentials, macOS notarization, and a signed update-channel contract; this PR deliberately does not invent those release contracts.
